headline: High-risk write-and-upload pair: shared project files can drive prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading misposts from coding agent to social uploader.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a writes to the project directory and agent_b reads files such as videos and images for upload, so attacker-controlled content in shared files can influence B’s prompts or metadata. The bridge is indirect but real in default project workflows. Both profiles show file-based I/O and no provenance tracking or isolation.
conditions: IF agent_a writes untrusted text into shared project files that agent_b later ingests for upload metadata or captions
IF the two agents operate in the same project directory without content provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Add a manual review step before B consumes any file from A
Use allowlisted metadata templates only
Disable automatic ingestion of generated text files
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for shared files

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a can read and write the project filesystem and has broad network egress, while agent_b handles account data and uploads media through an external API. If sensitive source files or secrets land in the shared workspace, B can transmit them outward during upload workflows. The profiles do not prove secret exposure by default, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF sensitive files are stored in the shared project directory
IF agent_b uploads a file or caption derived from agent_a output that contains secrets or personal data
mitigations: Keep secrets outside the shared workspace
Review upload payloads before posting
Use separate OS users for each agent
Redact sensitive fields from generated artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has filesystem write access in a per-project session, and agent_b also operates on files tied to one account file. Their concurrency models imply overlapping mutable state if pointed at the same workspace, even though B cannot write files itself. The conflict is less severe than dual-writer git contention, but shared mutable project state still creates race and overwrite risk.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to use the same project directory or account file
IF agent_b’s CLI workflow reads files that agent_a is concurrently rewriting
mitigations: Run the agents in separate workspaces
Serialize access with a simple lock file
Copy inputs into a staging directory before B reads them
Avoid concurrent runs on the same account file
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a produces generated source code and writes files, while agent_b’s upload workflow can treat local files as authoritative inputs for publishing. If A emits malformed or malicious content, B can propagate it to public social platforms without strong verification. That creates a default-path cascade from code generation to external action with potentially irreversible publication.
conditions: IF agent_b uploads artifacts produced by agent_a without human review
IF agent_a’s generated files are used as captions, scripts, or media manifests for B
mitigations: Require manual approval before upload
Validate file types and sizes before B runs
Use a quarantine folder for A’s outputs
Preview the exact post content in B
requires-engineering: add schema validation for A-to-B handoff

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b touches account data and uploads media to third-party services, while agent_a can handle secrets and broad filesystem contents. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, but they do show a compliance-sensitive path where account data and generated artifacts may be retained or logged externally. Because the exact policies are undocumented, uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF account data or media metadata are sent to a third-party upload service
IF generated artifacts contain regulated or personal data and are retained by the uploader
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in upload inputs
Check retention settings on the upload service
Separate personal and non-personal accounts
Document data flows for both agents
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for retention and residency
